newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Election gamble in FTSE index options.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Election gamble in FTSE index options.

text.p: The London equities options market remained relatively subdued on Tuesday, reflecting investors preference to stay out of the market until after the forthcoming election. One of the biggest deals of the day in equity options was counting on the market's continuing lethargy.
An investor executed a straddle trade in BG Plc, in which 2,000 December 180 calls and puts were sold for a joint cost of 35p, anticipating very little movement in the underlying share price.
The shares were down 2p at 181-1/2 by 1459 GMT.
"It means they are buyers of the stock at 145p and sellers at 215p," said one options specialist. "They think the stock is going nowhere."
In FTSE index options 12,000 May 4,575 contracts were bought at 2p.
"Its an interesting trade," said one trader. "They are betting on the market going up...it's an election gamble."
Elsewhere 500 October 650 puts in NatWest were bought for 21p and a strangle was executed in Tomkins, in which the investor sold 400 June 260 puts and 280 calls for a combined cost of 28p.
